title: Halcyon Drift Rising
premise: Xanthe Kavanagh, an insurance investigator whose job is to prove accidents were nobody's fault, is sent to Halcyon Drift, a decaying orbital colony that two rival fleets each believe the other destroyed years ago. Xanthe discovers the colony never died at all: its survivors, including a child who may be Xanthe's own erased past made flesh, have been kept alive by a forged manifest and a false casualty list that keeps both fleets from returning to finish their war. When an auditor's query exposes the impossible name on a ship that never flew, Xanthe must choose between certifying the lie that preserves the found family they've stumbled into or telling a truth that will bring both fleets down on Halcyon Drift. In the end, Xanthe files a third report—one that makes the colony officially exist again—sacrificing their own fabricated identity so the survivors can claim theirs.
about_author: I. M. Vasquez is the pen name of a former maritime claims adjuster who spent eleven years untangling disasters no one wanted to claim. They write near-future fiction about paperwork, grief, and the people who fall through bureaucratic cracks.

chapters.title: The Actuary of Small Disasters
chapters.summary: Xanthe Kavanagh arrives at Halcyon Drift to close a twenty-year-old file on a 'total loss' event, narrating in first person with dry professional detachment. The colony is supposed to be a tomb; instead they find lights, hydroponics, and a woman named Odile who greets them by a name Xanthe doesn't recognize. Emotional beat: unease beneath routine—the investigator realizes the accident report doesn't match anything real.

chapters.title: Manifest of the Never-Flew
chapters.summary: Digging through colonial records, Xanthe finds the evacuation ship Meridian logged as lost with all hands—yet its passenger list includes 'Xanthe Kavanagh,' age nine. POV alternates between Xanthe and Odile, who watches the stranger search and quietly decides what to hide. Emotional beat: vertigo; Xanthe's flawless identity begins to feel like someone else's forgery.

chapters.title: Children of the Quiet War
chapters.summary: Odile reveals the truth in fragments: after the fleets' battle crippled the drift, survivors faked total destruction to keep both sides away, maintaining the wreck like stagecraft for passing sensors. Xanthe meets the colony's children, born into the masquerade, including taciturn teen Rho who was told the outside world ended. Emotional beat: reluctant tenderness—Xanthe starts investigating less and belonging more.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Lie
chapters.summary: Through intercepted fleet traffic, Xanthe reconstructs the geopolitics: the Concord and the Verity Accord each blame the other for Halcyon's destruction, and the fragile armistice rests on that shared grief. If either learns the colony lives, war resumes over salvage rights and blame. POV: Xanthe alone, drafting reports they don't send. Emotional beat: dawning responsibility—the lie isn't hiding a crime, it's holding back a war.

chapters.title: What the Auditor Saw
chapters.summary: A Concord audit drone flags the impossible name on the Meridian manifest, and an auditor, Sef Amari, is dispatched to interview the 'deceased' investigator. Xanthe must perform being a living records clerk while Sef's questions circle closer. POV shifts to Sef, who suspects fraud but not its scale. Emotional beat: cat-and-mouse tension; Xanthe lies fluently and hates how good they've become at it.

chapters.title: Rho Runs the Numbers
chapters.summary: Rho, secretly self-taught in fleet cryptography, decrypts Sef's uplink and discovers the audit was triggered deliberately—someone inside the colony sold them out, hoping exposure would force rescue. Suspicion fractures the community; Odile defends the betrayer's motive. POV: Rho, fierce and frightened. Emotional beat: found family under strain—the masquerade protected them but also imprisoned them.

chapters.title: The Name I Was Given
chapters.summary: Xanthe confronts their own history: the child on the manifest was real, memory-wiped and reissued as an orphan investigator—a fleet program for disposable witnesses. Odile confirms she knew Xanthe's mother. POV: dual, Xanthe and Odile, memories overlapping. Emotional beat: grief and recognition—Xanthe's invisibility was engineered, and Halcyon is where it ends.

chapters.title: Deadline at Perihelion
chapters.summary: Sef Amari's report window closes in six days; when it lapses, both fleets receive the anomaly automatically. The colonists vote: run, fight, or tell the truth on their own terms. Xanthe proposes a third path—file a restoration charter making Halcyon a recognized neutral habitat, using their investigator credentials to certify it. Emotional beat: resolve forged from fear; the climax's machinery is set.

chapters.title: Everything True at Once
chapters.summary: Climax. As Sef moves to transmit the anomaly, Xanthe broadcasts the full record—battle footage, survivor lists, the forged manifest—to both fleets simultaneously, then submits the restoration charter with themselves listed as witness, not victim. Sef, moved by the children's testimony, delays the anomaly long enough for the charter to register. Emotional beat: terrifying honesty; the lie dies so everyone can live.

chapters.title: Halcyon Drift Rising
chapters.summary: Both fleets arrive—not as combatants but as claimants before a now-legal neutral port, forced to negotiate instead of shoot. Xanthe surrenders their old identity to the archives and takes residence papers signed 'Kavanagh, Xanthe, resident.' Rho asks what name they'll use next. Emotional beat: quiet homecoming—identity as something chosen, kept, and shared rather than assigned.
